findings.location: the project-settings section, project name form; the notification-settings section, digest frequency form
findings.evidence: The Save button in project-settings and the Submit button in notification-settings are present, with input fields for project name and digest frequency respectively. No result state, success message, error state, or next screen is defined for either form submission.
findings.violation: These state-changing form submissions commit the user's input to the system but do not specify what feedback the user receives (success message, error state, loading indicator, or result screen) while the action processes or after it completes.
findings.fix: For each form submission, define a result state the artifact shows after successful completion, such as a success message on the current screen, a result screen confirming the change, or a visual indication (color change, disabled state) that the change took effect.

findings.evidence: The invite-sent screen displays 'An invite was sent to the address entered above.' The only control offered is 'Back to project settings' link. No unsend, revoke, cancel, or withdraw option appears anywhere in the artifact after an invite is committed.
findings.violation: Sending an invite is a reasonably reversible action in collaboration products, but the artifact provides no reversal path. A user who sends an invite by mistake has no way within the design to retract it before the recipient accepts.
findings.fix: Add an unsend or revoke action on the invite-sent screen or on a subsequent pending-invitations management screen, so users can reverse a sent invite if needed.

findings.location: the project-settings section, the project-settings-save-btn button
findings.violation: This artifact uses 2 different labels for what reads as the same commit action: "Save", "Submit". A user cannot tell from the label alone whether these controls perform the same action or different ones.
findings.fix: Pick one label for this commit action, for example "Save", and use it everywhere the action appears.
